Md Khurshid Alam Khan, Advocate ------ For the Petitioner. 
Md Abdul Majid, Advocate ------ For the Opposite-Party Nos. 1-10.
parties:
Bank of Small Industries & Commerce Bangladesh   ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Shahabuddin Ahmed    ------ Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
Khondker Musa Khaled J: On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the order No. 35 dated 6-11-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Chittagong, in Misc, Case No. 404 of 2004 allowing the said case under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure, should not be set aside or such other order passed as this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The relevant facts necessary for disposal of the rule are that the. petitioner, namely Bank of Small Industries & Commerce Bangladesh (Now Basic Bank Ltd), as plaintiff, filed Money Suit No. 27 of 1994 for realization of Taka 2,38,63,639.03 (two crore thirty eight lac sixty three thousand six hundred thirty nine three paisa) against the defendants 1-3 alleging that the defendant No. 1 Md Moazzem Hossain, a businessman, opened several accounts in the petitioner-bank with false and fictitious names in collusion with two Bank employees - defendants 2-3 and they in collusion with each other misappropriated huge amount of Taka 6,53,656.58 (Six lack fifty three thousand six hundred fifty six fifty eight paisa) from the bank within a period from 2.8.1992 to 22-2-1995 by resorting to forgery and fraud. The defendants 2-3 had helped the defendant No. 1 to encash the forged and fraudulent cheques. All the vouchers and related documents of the Bank were signed by the Bank employees, defendants 2- 3. Since the defendants 1-3 did not appear in the Money Suit, the same was decreed exparte with costs on 7-7-1997. Thereafter, the decree holder- Bank put the decree in execution by filing Money Execution Case No.2 of 2002 in the Court of the Joint District Judge, First Court, Chittagong and on 7-8-2004, it was fixed for auction sale of the judgment debtor's property by an Order dated 23-6- 2004. During pendency of the execution case, the opposite-parties 4-13, as a 3rd party to the proceeding, filed Misc. Case No. 404 of 2004 under Order  XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure setting up a claim case on the attached property. The decree holder Bank filed a written objection praying for dismissal of the aforesaid claim case, but the learned Judge of the Executing Court, without proper investigation into the claim of ownership and possession, allowed the Misc. Case and released the attached property of the auction sale by the impugned judgment and Order dated 6-11-2004. 

 4. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner Bank (decree holder), submits, that the learned Judge of the Execution Court ought to have investigated into the claim of the 3rd party by taking necessary evidence as contemplated under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He submits that it is evident from the impugned judgment that neither any oral evidence was recorded nor any documents were admitted in evidence to lay foundation of his decision. So, the learned Advocate submits that the impugned judgment and order is apparently illegal and arbitrary as the statutory provisions in proving the case have not been complied with. As such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside. 

 5. Mr Md Abdul Majid, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite-party nos. 1-10 submits, in reply, that the revisional application against an order passed under Order XXI Rule 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure releasing the property from attachment is not at all maintainable, as such, an order is appealable under Order XLIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate submits further that the decree-holder's first execution case relating to the same money decree was filed earlier and it was dismissed on limitation ground. So, the 2nd execution case bearing No.2 of 2002, in which the impugned order of attachment was passed, is also barred under Article -182 of the law of limitation. In this respect, the learned Advocate has relied upon the case of Babul Chowdhury and others vs Reba Rani Saha and others reported in 15 BLD 644. It is submitted that through the defendant 2, one of the judgment-debtor, is full brother of the present opposite-parties, their deceased father namely Shamsuddin being owner of the disputed property excluded him from inheriting the paternal property by execution of a Notarised Wasiatnama. So, the opposite-parties have become exclusive owner and possessors of the property under attachment by inheritance and several transfers by the previous owner Sharnsuddin and some successive owners. As such, the property of the opposite-parties cannot be subject matter of the attachment in the execution case and it cannot be legally sold on auction in execution of money decree passed against the persons including the defendant No.2 AKM Nazimuddin, a son of the previous owner late Shamsuddin. Therefore, the impugned order, as has been passed by the learned Judge of the Court below, does not call for interference. 

 6. On perusal of the impugned judgment, it appears that the Court below has accepted the contentions of the opposite-parties (petitioners of Misc. Case) regarding "Wasiatnama", transfer by gift etc in toto without investigation as to the genuineness of the claim of ownership and exclusive possession of the said 3rd party members. It requires to be seen whether inheritance by a son from father can be legally nullified by execution of Notarized 'Wasiatnama". Moreover, execution of such deed is also required to be proved. Neither deposition of any witness was recorded nor the alleged documents of acquiring interest in the property by the claimant were admitted in evidence for consideration with necessary exhibit marks. As such, no legal evidence is available before us to examine whether the petitioners of the Misc. Case have acquired exclusive possession in the attached property of the Execution Case and whether they have been claiming property under any of the judgment-debtors and when they actually got possession in the attached property. 

 10. So far the question of limitation of the Execution Case is concerned, we hold the view that neither the particulars of the concerned Execution Case along with the date of money decree are available before us nor it is proper forum to decide the question of limitation in filling the execution Case No.2 of 2002. It may be noted here that we are concerned only with the question whether the impugned judgment and order as has been passed in Misc. Case No. 404 of 2004 under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure is legally sustainable or not. 

 11. Considering all the aspects of the case, we are inclined to hold that the leaned Judge of the Court below has committed gross illegality in passing the impugned judgment and order violating the specific statutory provisions of Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. So, he said judgment and order cannot legally be sustained. At the same time, the claim and objection case of the 3rd party cannot be thrown away and is required to be adjudicated further by taking evidence and to that end in view it is necessary to send back in Misc. Case on remand for taking proper decision after proper investigation by recording evidence. 

 12. In the result, the rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and order dated 6-11-2004 passed in Misc. Case No. 404 of 2004 under order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure arising out of the Execution Case No.2 of 2002, are hereby set aside. The Misc. Case No. 404 of 2004 is send back on remand to the concerned Court below for holding further investigation providing opportunity to the parties to examine witness and adduce documentary evidence in accordance with law and our observations made herein before. After obtaining necessary evidence to resolve the issues of the claim and objection case, the learned Judge shall pass a judgment afresh as expeditiously as possible preferably within 4 months from the date of receipt of the lower Court records.
